html:
The Boruca, or Brunka, are an Indigenous people of southern Costa Rica, in the hills near the Pacific coast. They speak, or once spoke, a Chibchan language, related to that of the Bribri.

In 1492 the region was home to chiefdoms that worked gold and carved the famous stone spheres of the Diquís delta. The Spanish founded a mission at Boruca in the 1600s, and the people mixed with others brought there. The Boruca are known for their carved and painted balsa masks and for the Fiesta de los Diablitos, held every New Year, in which masked "little devils" fight a bull that stands for the Spanish, and win. Their language has almost no native speakers left.
